subject.title: Feature: Per-spawn tool restrictions for sub-agents

question: Should OpenClaw expose per-spawn `sessions_spawn` tool restrictions as the open candidate PR's `toolsAllow` allowlist, or require a broader allow/deny policy shape before landing?
rationale: The implementation boundary is clear, but this becomes a public security-sensitive agent API and durable session-policy contract, so automation cannot choose the permanent semantics.

options.title: Land allowlist-first API
options.body: Accept `toolsAllow` as the additive V1 contract, with explicit empty-list, persistence, fail-closed unsupported-runtime behavior, docs, and tests.

options.title: Require allow/deny shape
options.body: Hold the candidate until the API supports both allow and deny semantics so it matches the original least-privilege proposal more directly.

options.title: Defer to broader permissions design
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers design one delegated tool-policy model across spawned sessions, bindings, skills, and request-time APIs.

recommendation.title: Land allowlist-first API
recommendation.body: Accept `toolsAllow` as the additive V1 contract, with explicit empty-list, persistence, fail-closed unsupported-runtime behavior, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is tied to the original `sessions_spawn` feature, sandbox inheritance hardening, and prior maintainer-facing review of this security boundary.
